items.markdown: mization problems will be developed. Furthermore, the SDP problems will be directly formulated in the format required by the SDP solver, thus avoiding the use of interfaces like *SOStools*. An open source toolbox will be then released. Second, by exploiting the probabilistic interpretation of set-membership estimation, we plan to reformulate it using the theory of moments developed by Lasserre. This will allow us to ground totally set-membership estimation in the realm of the probabilistic setting, which will give us the possibility of combining the two approaches in order to obtain hybrid filters, i.e., filters that include both classical probabilistic uncertainties and set-membership uncertainties.
